text:
Lia: thinking out loud — can we try an observer-lease pattern for active/active detection instead of full leader election?
Lia: idea is lightweight observers per region that only detect divergence and trigger a controlled demote/promote instead of hard swaps
Raj: curious — how do observers avoid false positives during transient network flaps?
Lia: we keep a two-phase confirmation: probe + quorum-of-observers + short jittered grace window (200-500ms)
Sam: ok but what about data residency constraints? we can't silently forward writes to a non-resident region even for failover
Maria: +1. residency must be enforced at the proxy layer. proxies should refuse cross-region writes if tenant flagged as "resident:" true
Dante: that implies the proxy needs to surface a deterministic failure mode to clients and operators, not an internal retry that rewrites elsewhere
Lia: exactly — failure semantics: 409/residency_violation with a hint header and optional retry-region suggestion
Lia: example header: `X-Residency-Reason: tenant-policy:eu_only`
Sam: can we avoid a big perf penalty by doing residency checks async? e.g., cache resident flag in proxy with short TTL and fallback to control-plane on miss
Maria: cache+TTL is fine but must be observable. add a proxy metric: residency_check_miss and residency_enforced_denied_count
Raj: back to observers — when observers detect a probable split, what's the safe demote sequence?
Lia: proposed sequence: 1) observer quorum signals probable split; 2) mark region in "isolated" state (routing prefers local reads only); 3) propagate a soft-demote marker to data plane; 4) allow reads, block cross-residency writes; 5) operator notification and automatic rollback window (configurable 30-300s)
Dante: step 3 needs a clear operator-visible signal so on-call can decide forced cutover vs wait. add a dedicated incident tag in console UI
Sam: how does this interact with KV cache ownership and prefix caching? if we mark soft-demote we must invalidate prefix cache that may have foreign residency scopes
Maria: we should attach residency stamps to cache entries: `residency:eu-west-1` and invalidate on demote transitions
Raj: what about long-lived sessions that keep routing to now-isolated region? do we need sticky-client hints to re-evaluate after a demote?
Lia: proxies must add `X-Region-Probe: must-revalidate` to sticky sessions for clients to re-resolve on next connect. mobile SDKs should respect 307-like steering hints
ops-bot: canary deployed observer service to eu-west-1 earlier today — no alerts so far :thumbsup:
Dante: we also need synthetic chaos tests: partition one region for 60s and validate observers trigger isolated state and residency enforcement prevents writes to wrong region
Sam: add a low-risk experiment: route 0.5% of traffic via observer-path only and measure false positive/recovery rates
Maria: also need audit trail: every demote decision must be logged with observer quorum IDs, timestamps, and the list of affected tenants
Lia: good point — tie that to the rollout system so we can roll back demote automation per-customer if needed
Raj: edge case — what if observer quorum itself is skewed because observability collectors are in the same failure domain? diversify observer placement across AZs and a second region mirror
Dante: and require at least one observer outside the region under test to confirm cross-region partitioning
Sam: operational knobs we need: grace_window_ms, observer_quorum_size, auto_demote_enabled (per-tenant toggle), residency_cache_ttl, demote_rollback_window_s
Maria: can we provide a compatibility shim for existing proxies: honor X-Preferred-Region header but reject if residency mismatch and include `X-Residency-Action: deny`
Lia: next steps: write a short RFC with the state machine diagram + metrics list + runbook snippets. I'll draft and ping this thread for review
Raj: 👍 please include exact HTTP error payloads and headers so SDKs can wire behavior
Dante: I'll sketch the SRE runbook and chaos tests after the RFC draft
Sam: I'll prototype the proxy residency cache and expose metrics
Maria: I'll add cache residency stamps to the KV cache proposal and update the cache invalidation logic
Lia: thanks all — big win if we can get safe automated detection without breaking residency guarantees
Lia: tagging for RFC follow-up: @here :eyes:
